subject: microbiology
title: Ascaris lumbricoides, Loeffler Syndrome and Hookworm Anaemia

steps.tx: The giant intestinal roundworm **Ascaris lumbricoides** is the most prevalent helminthic parasite of humans, inhabiting the lumen of the small intestine. Transmission occurs through ingestion of embryonated eggs from fecally contaminated soil, water, or raw vegetables. Ingested eggs hatch in the duodenum, releasing rhabditiform larvae that penetrate the mesenteric venules to begin an obligate heart-lung systemic migration.
steps.say: Ingested embryonated eggs hatch in the duodenum, releasing larvae that migrate through the lungs.

vis.caption: Ascaris lumbricoides life cycle illustrating pulmonary larval transit and intestinal maturation [Credit: CDC, StewardMD cleared]

steps.tx: During alveolar transit ten to fourteen days after ingestion, migrating larvae break through pulmonary capillaries into alveolar airspaces, provoking acute hypersensitivity pneumonitis known as **Loeffler syndrome**. Patients present with low-grade fever, dry non-productive cough, wheezing, and marked peripheral blood eosinophilia. Chest radiography reveals characteristic fleeting, transient, non-segmental infiltrates that migrate across pulmonary zones over days.
steps.say: Larval rupture into alveoli causes Loeffler syndrome with fleeting migratory pulmonary infiltrates and eosinophilia.

left.title: Loeffler syndrome (pulmonary phase)
points: Occurs 1 to 2 weeks following egg ingestion
Larvae rupture into alveoli causing inflammation

right.title: Intestinal ascariasis (adult phase)
points: Develops 2 to 3 months later in jejunum
Adults live free in lumen feeding on chyme
Mechanical bowel obstruction in heavy load
Eosinophilia usually absent or mild in adults

steps.tx: Adult worms measure twenty to thirty-five centimetres in length and live unattached within the jejunal lumen. In young children with high worm burdens, entangled masses of adult worms can precipitate acute mechanical **intestinal obstruction**, typically wedged at the narrow ileocaecal valve. Worms may also wander into the ampulla of Vater, causing acute biliary colic, obstructive jaundice, ascending bacterial cholangitis, or acute pancreatitis.
steps.say: Entangled masses of giant roundworms can mechanically obstruct the ileocaecal valve or invade the common bile duct.

rows: Ampulla of Vater and common bile duct
Midgut loop twisted by worm weight
Surgical resection of non-viable bowel segment

steps.tx: Fecal examination demonstrates characteristic fertilized eggs measuring sixty by forty-five micrometres with a thick, golden-brown, bile-stained shell covered by an irregular, bumpy, tuberculated **mammillated albuminous coat**. Unfertilized eggs are longer and narrower with a disorganized internal yolk. Stool microscopy also identifies hookworm eggs, which are thin-shelled, colorless, and contain segmented blastomeres.
steps.say: Golden-brown fertilized eggs with a thick tuberculated mammillated coat are easily identified on stool microscopy.

vis.caption: Ascaris lumbricoides fertilized egg showing thick shell with golden-brown mammillated albuminous coat [Credit: CDC, StewardMD cleared]

steps.tx: Human hookworm infection is caused by **Ancylostoma duodenale** (the Old World hookworm) and Necator americanus (the New World hookworm). Filariform larvae in contaminated warm soil penetrate bare human feet, causing a pruritic, erythematous, papulovesicular dermatitis known as ground itch or dew sores. After vascular transport and pulmonary transit, adult worms attach to the mucosal brush border of the upper small intestine.
steps.say: Soil filariform larvae penetrate bare feet causing ground itch before migrating to the small intestine.

left.title: Ancylostoma duodenale
points: Buccal capsule bears two pairs of sharp curved teeth
Blood loss: 0.15 to 0.20 millilitres per worm daily
Can be transmitted orally via contaminated water

right.title: Necator americanus
points: Buccal capsule bears a pair of semilunar cutting plates
Blood loss: 0.03 to 0.05 millilitres per worm daily
Lacks arrested larval dormancy in human tissues

steps.tx: The adult hookworm anchors firmly to mucosal villi using its heavily armed buccal capsule: Ancylostoma duodenale possesses two pairs of sharp chitinous **ventral teeth**, whereas Necator americanus possesses a pair of semilunar cutting plates. The worm actively lacerates villous capillaries, secreting anticoagulant peptides that inhibit factor Xa and platelet aggregation to maintain continuous blood suction for feeding.
steps.say: Chitinous teeth lacerate mucosal capillaries, secreting anticoagulants to sustain continuous blood feeding.

steps.tx: Chronic unreplaced intestinal blood loss produces severe **hookworm anaemia**, characterized by microcytic hypochromic iron deficiency anaemia accompanied by hypoalbuminaemia and peripheral oedema. Patients present with profound lethargy, exertional dyspnoea, koilonychia, and pica. A burden of just one hundred Ancylostoma worms extracts twenty millilitres of blood daily, exhausting iron stores rapidly in malnourished children.
steps.say: Continuous blood loss exhausts iron stores, precipitating severe microcytic hypochromic hookworm anaemia.

nodes.label: Adult hookworms suck blood continuously from jejunal mucosa
Chronic daily blood loss exceeds dietary iron intake
Progressive depletion of iron stores leads to severe microcytic hypochromic anaemia

steps.tx: First-line anthelmintic therapy for both ascariasis and hookworm infection is a single oral dose of **albendazole** (four hundred milligrams) or mebendazole (five hundred milligrams), which selectively binds nematode beta-tubulin to inhibit microtubule polymerisation. In mass drug administration campaigns in endemic schools, annual or biannual deworming combined with oral iron supplementation successfully reverses growth stunting and cognitive deficits.
steps.say: Single dose albendazole binds beta tubulin to clear both roundworms and hookworms effectively.
